title: Adult Upper-Airway Emergency: Stridor, Epiglottitis and Airway Escalation

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult stridor and suspected rapidly progressive upper-airway obstruction; stabilisation and airway-team escalation.
findings: Rebuilt against the approved-topic structure: a tiered investigation panel, time-ordered management and an explicit medicine decision pathway.
Every investigation row includes a reference or normal state, condition finding and next action.
Previous outline and published rows remain preserved; this additive version is pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was found in the opened Saudi Ministry of Health protocol index unless a Saudi source is explicitly cited in the medicine row.
Current live Saudi Food and Drug Authority product registration was not individually confirmed; clinicians must check the hospital formulary.
Local antibiogram, resistance pattern, shared-care agreement and imaging availability require site-level confirmation where relevant.

pathophysiology.summary: Laryngeal or supraglottic oedema narrows the fixed upper airway. Turbulent inspiratory flow produces stridor. Fatigue or complete obstruction can abruptly remove effective airflow.
keyMechanisms: Laryngeal or supraglottic oedema narrows the fixed upper airway.
Fatigue or complete obstruction can abruptly remove effective airflow.

symptoms: Noisy breathing, throat pain, dysphagia, odynophagia, voice change or inability to handle secretions.
physicalSigns: Inspiratory stridor, drooling, tripod posture, accessory-muscle use or reduced air entry.
redFlags: Silent airway, cyanosis, exhaustion, altered consciousness, severe work of breathing or rapidly progressive swelling.
precipitants: Infection, anaphylaxis, inhalation injury, foreign body, tumour, post-procedural swelling or neck haematoma.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Acute airway compromise with urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm or hypotension.
Predominantly expiratory wheeze rather than inspiratory stridor.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Stridor indicates partial but clinically important upper-airway obstruction; a silent airway with respiratory effort suggests complete obstruction.

ruleIn.normalValue: Quiet breathing, normal voice and secretion handling
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Stridor, drooling, muffled voice, reduced airflow or fatigue
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: The trend determines urgency; a quieter airway can mean worsening airflow, not recovery.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports cause and severity but cannot exclude dangerous supraglottic disease.

clinicalManagement.title: Call the airway team
actions: Summon senior anaesthesia, otolaryngology and critical care; move to a fully equipped airway location.
Keep the patient upright and calm; avoid unnecessary supine positioning or throat instrumentation.

clinicalManagement.title: Maintain oxygenation
actions: Prepare a primary and rescue airway plan with front-of-neck access capability.

clinicalManagement.title: Secure or observe the airway
actions: Use the named airway lead's plan; preserve spontaneous ventilation when the team judges loss of the airway likely after induction.
Transfer only with an airway-capable escort and equipment.

branches.label: Anaphylaxis with upper-airway compromise
branches.entryCriteria: Acute airway, breathing or circulation compromise consistent with anaphylaxis

branches.label: Suspected bacterial epiglottitis
branches.entryCriteria: Stable enough for antimicrobial treatment after immediate airway-team control planning

medicationPlan.note: Airway control takes priority. These branches are cause-specific and must not be combined automatically. Current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed; check the hospital formulary.

regimens.patientGroup: Adult with anaphylaxis and upper-airway compromise
regimens.frequency: Repeat every 5–15 minutes if airway, breathing or circulation problems persist
regimens.duration: Continue repeated doses while the emergency response is activated; refractory cases require a monitored specialist infusion pathway
adjustments: Use age/weight-specific dosing for children; this row is adult only.
Do not delay for intravenous access.
Check hospital formulary; current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Continuous airway, breathing, circulation, oxygen saturation and cardiac rhythm.
Record response and time of every dose.
contraindications: No absolute contraindication in life-threatening anaphylaxis.
Intravenous bolus epinephrine is not this regimen and requires an experienced specialist setting.
regimens.sourceTitle: Saudi Ministry of Health Anaphylaxis Protocol
regimens.sourceEdition: Saudi MOH Anaphylaxis Protocol, Section emergency treatment algorithm

regimens.indication: Empirical treatment after airway planning for suspected bacterial epiglottitis
regimens.duration: 7–10 days; narrow to microbiology and specialist advice
adjustments: Seek microbiology advice for severe beta-lactam allergy.
Review hepatic and renal function when both are severely impaired.
Ceftriaxone is listed in the Saudi Essential Medicines List; current live SFDA registration was not individually confirmed.
monitoring: Airway status continuously; temperature and inflammatory response daily.
Blood-culture result, adverse effects and liver/renal profile.
contraindications: Do not delay definitive airway management to give antibiotics.

teaching.scope: Adult stridor and suspected rapidly progressive upper-airway obstruction; stabilisation and airway-team escalation.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Silent airway, cyanosis, exhaustion, altered consciousness, severe work of breathing or rapidly progressive swelling.
Use the named airway lead's plan; preserve spontaneous ventilation when the team judges loss of the airway likely after induction.
pitfalls: Stopping after a short outline instead of documenting the full investigation pathway.
Using a medicine row without checking the branch, allergy, organ function, culture result and local formulary.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval; this version remains pending until a clinician approves it.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: No emergency-department discharge while stridor or significant supraglottic pathology persists; disposition must be agreed by the airway team.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Document the cause, definitive airway plan, critical-care location and specialist follow-up.
